test_cases.test_name: Functional Test: Chart Creation and Nelson Rules Application
test_cases.objective: To verify that the SPC dashboard can correctly create X-bar/R and p-charts from a CSV file and apply the vendor's standard Nelson rules for statistical process control.
prerequisites: SPC Dashboard software is installed and accessible
Valid CSV test file with sample QC data is available
User account with 'Analyst' role permissions is created

test_steps.action: Log into the SPC dashboard using the pre-configured 'Analyst' role user credentials.
test_steps.expected_result: User successfully authenticates and the main dashboard interface loads without errors.

test_steps.action: Navigate to the 'Create New Chart' function and select the option to import data from a CSV file.
test_steps.expected_result: The system displays the file browser dialog for CSV file selection.

test_steps.action: Select the pre-prepared test CSV file containing 1000 data points for QC measurements and confirm the import.
test_steps.expected_result: The system processes the file and displays a preview of the data without errors.

test_steps.action: Select the chart type 'X-bar/R' and configure the necessary parameters (subgroup size, specifications).
test_steps.expected_result: The system generates the X-bar and R control charts based on the imported data.

test_steps.action: Enable the vendor's standard Nelson rules from the chart configuration options.
test_steps.expected_result: The system applies the Nelson rules, and any out-of-control points are visually flagged on the chart.

test_steps.action: Repeat steps 4-5 for a p-chart using attribute data from the CSV file.
test_steps.expected_result: The system correctly generates a p-chart with Nelson rules applied.
data_to_capture: List of triggered rules for the p-chart

test_steps.action: Use the built-in annotation feature to add a comment to an out-of-control point on the X-bar chart.
test_steps.expected_result: The comment is successfully saved and displayed on the chart.

acceptance_criteria: X-bar/R and p-charts are generated accurately from the CSV data input.
Vendor's standard Nelson rules are correctly applied and flag appropriate data points.
Chart annotations can be successfully created and saved.
No system errors or crashes occur during the test.
regulatory_basis: 21 CFR Part 211 - Current Good Manufacturing Practice for Finished Pharmaceuticals
FDA Guidance on Process Validation: General Principles and Practices
data_integrity_requirements: Imported data must be accurately represented in the generated charts.
Chart configurations and annotations must be saved correctly.
urs_requirements: URS-020-001: Users shall create X-bar/R and p-charts from CSV inputs.
URS-020-002: Users shall apply vendor's standard Nelson rules.
URS-020-005: Users shall annotate points with comments using built-in features.

test_cases.test_name: Performance and Integration Test: Data Loading and Export
test_cases.objective: To verify that the SPC dashboard meets performance requirements for loading large datasets and can successfully export reports to PDF and CSV formats.
prerequisites: SPC Dashboard software is installed and accessible
Large test CSV file with 100,000 data points is available
User account with 'Viewer' role permissions is created
Valid email account configured for scheduled reports

test_steps.action: Log into the SPC dashboard using the pre-configured 'Viewer' role user credentials.
test_steps.expected_result: User successfully authenticates and the main dashboard interface loads.

test_steps.action: Navigate to the data import function and select the large test CSV file containing 100,000 data points.
test_steps.expected_result: The system begins processing the file immediately after selection.

test_steps.action: Time the duration from file selection completion until the data is fully loaded and available for charting.
test_steps.expected_result: Data loading completes in less than 5 seconds as per performance requirement.

test_steps.action: Apply a filter to the loaded dataset (e.g., date range, product code) and time the chart rendering.
test_steps.expected_result: Charts re-render with the filtered data in less than 2 seconds.

test_steps.action: Export the current chart view to PDF format using the vendor's standard export function.
test_steps.expected_result: A PDF file is generated and downloaded successfully, containing the chart and relevant data.

test_steps.action: Export the underlying dataset to CSV format using the vendor's standard export function.
test_steps.expected_result: A CSV file is generated and downloaded, containing the complete dataset in the correct format.
data_to_capture: Exported CSV file for data integrity check

test_steps.action: Access the vendor's scheduler feature and configure a scheduled report email for the current chart.
test_steps.expected_result: The scheduled report is successfully configured without errors.

acceptance_criteria: 100,000 data points are loaded in less than 5 seconds.
Charts re-render in less than 2 seconds after filter changes.
PDF and CSV exports are generated correctly and contain accurate data.
Scheduled report configuration is successful.
regulatory_basis: 21 CFR Part 11 - Electronic Records; Electronic Signatures
Annex 11 - Computerized Systems
data_integrity_requirements: Exported data must match the source data exactly.
Performance metrics must be consistently met to ensure system usability.
urs_requirements: URS-020-003: The system shall provide vendor standard export to PDF and CSV.
URS-020-006: The system shall support scheduled report emails using vendor scheduler.
URS-020-010: Load 100k data points in < 5 seconds on supported hardware.
URS-020-011: Render charts in < 2 seconds after filter changes.

test_cases.test_name: Data Import and Chart Creation Verification
test_cases.objective: Verify the system can successfully import data from CSV and ODBC sources and create X-bar/R and p-charts as specified in the URS.
prerequisites: System installation is complete and verified (OQ-001)
Test user accounts with appropriate permissions are created
Test CSV files with valid SPC data are prepared
ODBC data source is configured and accessible

test_steps.action: Log into the SPC dashboard using valid credentials with chart creation permissions.
test_steps.expected_result: User successfully authenticates and gains access to the dashboard main interface.

test_steps.action: Navigate to the data import section and select CSV import option. Upload the prepared test CSV file containing 1000 data points.
test_steps.expected_result: System accepts the CSV file and displays a confirmation message indicating successful import.

test_steps.action: Select the imported dataset and initiate creation of an X-bar/R chart using the vendor's standard chart creation wizard.
test_steps.expected_result: System generates an X-bar/R chart displaying the control limits, data points, and center line correctly.

test_steps.action: Repeat the process to create a p-chart using a different attribute from the same dataset.
test_steps.expected_result: System successfully generates a p-chart with appropriate binomial control limits displayed.

test_steps.action: Navigate to the ODBC import option and connect to the pre-configured data source. Import a dataset of 500 records.
test_steps.expected_result: System establishes connection and imports data successfully from the ODBC source.

acceptance_criteria: All data imports complete without errors
X-bar/R and p-charts are generated correctly according to statistical standards
Control limits are calculated accurately based on the imported data
Import performance meets the requirement of loading 100k points in <5 seconds (scaled for test data)
regulatory_basis: FDA 21 CFR Part 11 for electronic records
GMP requirements for data integrity in quality control processes
data_integrity_requirements: Imported data must maintain accuracy and completeness
Chart calculations must be mathematically correct and reproducible
All data transformations must be traceable
urs_requirements: URS-020-001: Users shall create X-bar/R and p-charts from CSV inputs
URS-020-012: Import data from CSV and ODBC connections using standard connectors

test_cases.test_name: Nelson Rules Application and Export Functionality Test
test_cases.objective: Verify the system correctly applies vendor-standard Nelson rules to control charts and exports results to PDF and CSV formats as required.
prerequisites: OQ-003 has been successfully executed
Test charts with known Nelson rule violations are available
Export directories with write permissions are configured

test_steps.action: Open a pre-existing X-bar chart that contains data points designed to trigger specific Nelson rules (e.g., points beyond 3 sigma, runs, trends).
test_steps.expected_result: Chart displays with Nelson rule violations clearly marked according to vendor's standard visualization.

test_steps.action: Verify each triggered Nelson rule by examining the data points and comparing to the rule definitions in vendor documentation.
test_steps.expected_result: All Nelson rule applications are mathematically correct and consistent with statistical definitions.

test_steps.action: Select the export to PDF function and save the chart with Nelson rule violations to a specified directory.
test_steps.expected_result: System generates a PDF file containing the chart image, data summary, and Nelson rule violations report.

test_steps.action: Select the export to CSV function and export the underlying chart data including Nelson rule flags.
test_steps.expected_result: System generates a CSV file containing all data points, calculated statistics, and Nelson rule violation indicators.

test_steps.action: Open the exported files in their respective applications and verify content accuracy and completeness.
test_steps.expected_result: Exported files contain all expected data and formatting is maintained during the export process.
data_to_capture: Verification results for each export format
Any data corruption or formatting issues

acceptance_criteria: Nelson rules are applied correctly and consistently across all chart types
Export functions generate files with complete and accurate data representation
PDF exports maintain chart visual quality and include all necessary annotations
CSV exports contain all data points and calculated values without corruption
regulatory_basis: FDA 21 CFR Part 11 requirements for electronic records and signatures
ICH Q9 Quality Risk Management principles
data_integrity_requirements: Nelson rule calculations must be mathematically accurate
Export functions must preserve data integrity without alteration
Exported files must be complete and readable by standard applications
urs_requirements: URS-020-002: Users shall apply vendor's standard Nelson rules
URS-020-003: The system shall provide vendor standard export to PDF and CSV

test_cases.test_name: ODBC Data Import and Chart Generation Verification
test_cases.objective: To verify that the SPC dashboard can successfully import data from an ODBC data source and generate accurate control charts from the imported dataset.
prerequisites: OQ-001 completed successfully
ODBC data source configured and accessible
Valid dataset available in ODBC source
User with appropriate import permissions logged in

test_steps.action: Navigate to the data import section and select the ODBC connection option.
test_steps.expected_result: System displays ODBC connection configuration dialog with connection parameters.

test_steps.action: Configure the ODBC connection using pre-defined connection parameters and test the connection.
test_steps.expected_result: System confirms successful connection to the ODBC data source.

test_steps.action: Select a dataset from the ODBC source containing at least 100 data points for SPC analysis.
test_steps.expected_result: System displays available tables/views from the ODBC source for selection.

test_steps.action: Map the dataset columns to the required SPC chart fields (subgroup, measurement, etc.).
test_steps.expected_result: System accepts column mappings and validates data types are appropriate.

test_steps.action: Generate an X-bar/R chart using the imported ODBC data and apply Nelson rules.
test_steps.expected_result: System generates accurate control chart with proper control limits and applies Nelson rule violations correctly.

acceptance_criteria: ODBC connection establishes successfully without errors
Data imports completely with no data loss or corruption
Control chart calculations match manual verification calculations
All Nelson rules are applied correctly to the imported data
regulatory_basis: FDA 21 CFR Part 11 for electronic records integrity
ICH Q9 for quality risk management of data sources
data_integrity_requirements: Data must maintain integrity during ODBC transfer process
All imported data values must match source system values
Audit trail must record data source and import timestamp if supported

test_cases.test_name: Scheduled Report Generation and Email Distribution
test_cases.objective: To verify that the vendor's scheduler functionality correctly generates and distributes scheduled reports via email to designated recipients.
prerequisites: OQ-003 completed successfully
Email server configuration completed
Test email accounts configured for recipients
Valid chart configuration saved

test_steps.action: Access the vendor's scheduling feature and create a new scheduled report job.
test_steps.expected_result: Scheduling interface opens with options for frequency, recipients, and report format.

test_steps.action: Configure the schedule to run immediately for testing purposes, selecting PDF format and multiple test recipient emails.
test_steps.expected_result: System accepts schedule configuration and shows scheduled job in queue.

test_steps.action: Monitor the scheduler execution and verify the report generation process.
test_steps.expected_result: Scheduler executes the job at the scheduled time and generates the PDF report.

test_steps.action: Verify that email notifications are sent to all configured recipients with the correct attachments.
test_steps.expected_result: All designated recipients receive email with properly formatted PDF attachment.

test_steps.action: Validate the generated PDF report content matches the current chart configuration and data.
test_steps.expected_result: PDF report contains accurate chart images, statistics, and data matching the source.

acceptance_criteria: Scheduled report generates at the specified time without manual intervention
All configured recipients receive the email with correct attachments
Generated PDF report accurately represents the current chart data and configuration
Scheduler maintains job history and status tracking
regulatory_basis: FDA 21 CFR Part 11 for automated processes and electronic records
GMP requirements for automated reporting systems
data_integrity_requirements: Scheduled reports must maintain data accuracy and integrity
Email distribution must be complete and accurate to all recipients
Report content must be consistent with source data
